skill.name: Precise word for a vague one
skill.why: Vague words like nice make readers guess. A precise word shows what you mean.
skill.how: Spot the vague word. Hunt for clues. Pick the word that fits every clue.

steps.say: My soup was nice. Nice how? You can't tell!

show.nudge: Soup is exact. You know what it is. Which word could mean almost anything?
'Was' just links the words. Which word could mean lots of things?

steps.win: Yes! Nice could mean hot, tasty, salty... The reader has to guess.

steps.say: So I hunt for clues. What did the soup actually do?

show.nudge: 'It' just means the soup. Which part says what the soup did?
That is the weather. What did the soup do to me?

steps.ask: Tap the part that says what the soup did.
steps.win: Yes! That's a clue. Clues tell me what 'nice' really means.

steps.say: Now I try some words. Each one has to fit every clue.

options.reason: Chilled means cold. Did the soup make me colder?
Lumpy is about how it felt in your mouth. Which word fits warming you up?

steps.win: Yes! Warming fits every clue. That is the precise word.

steps.say: Careful! The fanciest word isn't always the precise one. Check it against the clue.

options.reason: Microscopic means too small to see without a microscope. Can you see the puppy?
Short is about how tall something is. The clue is about the whole puppy.

steps.win: Yes! Tiny fits the clue. Microscopic sounds clever, but it says something untrue.

steps.say: Vague nouns hide things too. 'Thing' and 'stuff' could be anything.

show.text: It had a long handle and soft bristles for painting.

options.reason: A pencil has no bristles. Check the clue again.
A mop has a handle, but do you paint with it?

steps.win: Yes! Brush is precise. It names exactly what she grabbed.

steps.say: Some words name things more exactly than others. Each one narrows it down.

show.nudge: Animal could be anything from a worm to a whale. Which names one exact kind?
Bird could be any bird at all. Which names one exact kind?

steps.win: Yes! A rainbow lorikeet is one exact kind of bird. The reader can picture it.

terms.means: Could mean lots of things: nice, good, bad, thing, stuff.
Words nearby that tell you what the writer really means.
Means one exact thing, and fits every clue.

encounters.frame: Mo is writing a review of his own cooking. Again.
encounters.text: Mo's pie was bad. The middle was still frozen solid.
encounters.prompt: Which word says exactly what was wrong with the pie?
encounters.success: Undercooked. A frozen middle means it wasn't cooked for long enough.

options.reason: Burnt means cooked for too long. Would a burnt pie still be frozen in the middle?
Soggy means wet and floppy. Frozen solid means hard.

parts.reason: Score is precise. It names exactly what Zed got.
Final is precise. It tells you exactly which round.

options.reason: A giraffe has a long neck, not a trunk.

encounters.frame: Indi is writing about her first swim of the year.

options.reason: Cool means only a little cold. Cool water wouldn't make your toes go numb straight away.
Lukewarm means a bit warm. It wouldn't make anyone's toes go numb.

encounters.frame: Gus is writing up what he found under his bed.

encounters.frame: Gus left his footy socks in the rain overnight.

options.reason: Damp means only a little wet. Water wouldn't pour out of a damp sock.
Moist means slightly wet. Water wouldn't splash all over the floor.
Humid describes air that feels heavy with water, not a sock.

options.reason: Silent means no sound at all. Zed could hear it, just barely.
Shrill means high and piercing. You wouldn't need to hold your breath to hear it.
Booming means loud and deep. Zed could hardly hear this noise.
